# leicht

> A tiny classless-first CSS library in modern CSS. Link one stylesheet, write ordinary HTML,
> and the page is styled. 6.8 kB gzipped, no build step, no dependencies, no !important.

Install: `npm i leicht` — or link `dist/leicht.min.css` directly.
Optional skins: `dist/leicht-themes.min.css` (1.6 kB, six looks via `data-skin`).

## How it works

- Semantic HTML is styled with no classes: headings, tables, forms, `<nav>`, `<article>` as a
  card, `<dialog>` as a modal, `[popover]` menus, `popover="hint"` tooltips, `<progress>`,
  `<meter>`, and `role="switch"` checkboxes.
- An application layer, also without classes, keyed on the markup that makes it accessible:
  `<aside>` as a child of `<body>` is an app shell (add `popover` to it for an off-canvas drawer
  below 60rem, opened by a `popovertarget` button with no JavaScript); `<figure>` around a
  `<table>` is a scrolling data table with `<figcaption>` as its caption row; `aside nav` is a
  vertical sidebar nav; `[role=tablist]` with `[role=tab][aria-selected]` is tabs; `<output>` as
  a child of `<body>` is a toast stack; `[aria-busy=true]` is a skeleton, or a spinner on a
  button; `<nav aria-label>` around an `<ol>` is pagination; `<dl>` is a key/value grid;
  `<td class="num">` or `<td><data value>` is a right-aligned numeric cell.
- A small set of classes covers what HTML has no element for: `.row`/`.col-N`, `.card`,
  `.button` + variants (`.secondary`, `.outline`, `.ghost`, `.error`, `.success`, `.warning`,
  `.neutral`), `.sm`/`.lg` sizes, `.alert`, `.group`, `.tag`, `.field` (an input row that can
  hold a prefix, icon or unit suffix), `.avatar`, `.dot`, `.carousel`, `.glass`, `.liquid`, and
  utilities including `.between`, `.end` and `.truncate`.
- Everything ships inside `@layer leicht.base, leicht.components, leicht.utilities`, so unlayered
  author CSS always wins — overriding never needs `!important`.
- All styling is tokens (`--l-*`). `--l-primary` takes a brand colour; `--l-hue` re-tints
  neutrals and accent together. The palette is OKLCH with fixed lightness, so a hue change cannot
  break contrast — `--l-primary`, `--l-error`, `--l-success` and `--l-warning` all measure
  between 4.8:1 and 5.1:1 against the page, checked by `test/contrast.test.mjs`.
- `--l-space` is a single density knob: layout spacing derives from it through
  `--l-space-xs/sm/md/lg/xl`, so one change compacts or loosens every component. Component
  interiors stay in `em`, so they scale with their own font size — which is why `.sm`/`.lg` need
  only set `font-size`. Other application tokens: `--l-aside`, `--l-table-max`, `--l-focus`, and
  `--l-width: none` to opt out of the 72rem measure.
- Dark mode is `light-dark()` plus `color-scheme` — no JavaScript. `data-theme` forces it;
  `data-skin` selects a skin; the two compose.

## Bleeding-edge CSS, used as progressive enhancement

corner-shape, border-shape, background-clip: border-area, anchor positioning with
position-try-fallbacks, anchored container queries, appearance: base-select with ::picker(select),
scroll-driven animations, @container scroll-state, ::scroll-marker, ::details-content,
@starting-style, sibling-index(), typed attr(), contrast-color(), text-box, CSS Custom Highlight
API, and liquid-glass refraction from a data-URI SVG filter. Each degrades to the plain look.
